verdict: Sound, kind and orthodox, and audibly machine-shaped: no contractions in 35,000 words meant to be spoken, an 'is not ... It is ...' pair in nearly half the pieces, a slogan at the end of most reflections, and one mould for all 72 devotions. Thanksgiving week shows what the library sounds like when it is his.

patterns.name: No contractions anywhere
patterns.note: 35,465 words of prose written to be read aloud to children contain zero contractions ("do not", "cannot", "it is", "you are" every time; "cannot" alone 67 times). This is the single loudest machine tell in the library. Fix as a pass, by ear, across reflection, questions, activity, prayer, grownups.line and catechism commentary. Leave passageText and scriptureText untouched, leave the formal catechism `answer` and `kidsAnswer` fields uncontracted (they are memorised), and keep a full "do not" or "is not" where the sentence leans on it. Roughly two in three should contract.

examples.why: 35,000 words meant to be read aloud to children hold not one contraction. No parent says "you do not have to" at the table; the ear hears a machine or a legal notice. VOICE-JAMES-BELL.md prefers contractions where they make prose sound spoken.

patterns.name: Aphoristic closers
patterns.note: Most reflections end on a slogan that restates the paragraph. Cut the slogan and let the paragraph end on its last concrete sentence.

examples.quote: And because he lives, the worst thing is never the last thing.
examples.replacement: And because he lives, death will not keep anyone who belongs to him.
examples.tell: Uncredited stock line used as the Easter closer
examples.why: "The worst thing is never the last thing" is a well-known line usually credited to Frederick Buechner. Here it runs unattributed as James's own closing sentence, on the most important day in the library.

examples.quote: If that is how the greatest one acted, then greatness in his family will always look like serving, never like being served. Real love kneels down.
examples.replacement: If that is how the greatest one acted, then greatness in his family will always look like serving, never like being served.
examples.why: The reflection ends by restating itself as a slogan. Most of the 72 devotions and many Advent days close this way, so the ear learns to expect the bow.

examples.quote: The question is less try harder and more stay connected. Healthy roots, good fruit.

examples.why: The reflection ends by restating itself as a slogan. Most of the 72 devotions and many Advent days close this way, so the ear learns to expect the bow. "Healthy roots, good fruit" is a verbless bumper sticker.

patterns.note: "actually" 40, "really" 36, "just" 85, "single" 16, "honest/honestly" 28, "on purpose" 18. Delete on sight unless the word is doing contrastive work.

patterns.name: Stacked superlatives
patterns.note: "deepest" 9 times, "most important" 10, "the strongest/hardest/most ... thing a person can do" 4. Say the thing at its true size.

examples.quote: It is the strongest, hardest, most God like thing a person can do.
examples.replacement: It is hard, and it is what God is like.
examples.why: "The most/deepest/strongest thing a person can ..." recurs ("deepest" 9 times, "most important" 10). Superlatives with no concrete case are the vague-intensifier tell, and a skeptic hears overclaim. Also a forced triplet and a missing hyphen.

examples.quote: Waiting on God turns out to be one of the strongest things a person can do.
examples.replacement: That kind of waiting takes strength.
examples.why: "The most/deepest/strongest thing a person can ..." recurs ("deepest" 9 times, "most important" 10). Superlatives with no concrete case are the vague-intensifier tell, and a skeptic hears overclaim.

examples.quote: For anyone raised without a good father, this is the deepest healing there is.
examples.replacement: For anyone raised without a good father, this can heal a great deal.
examples.why: "The most/deepest/strongest thing a person can ..." recurs ("deepest" 9 times, "most important" 10). Superlatives with no concrete case are the vague-intensifier tell, and a skeptic hears overclaim. On this subject especially the line should not overpromise; see the note to James.

patterns.name: Accuracy, care, consistency and mechanics
patterns.note: Individual defects: a misread passage, an overclaim, wording that does not match the printed passage, a typo, a self-contradiction between the Trinity activity and Q76, missing hyphens, a care gap, literary headings.

examples.quote: Most shepherds run when the wolf comes.
examples.replacement: The hired hand runs when the wolf comes.
examples.why: John 10:12-13 says the hired hand runs, in contrast with the shepherd. "Most shepherds run" is not what Jesus said and undercuts his own image.

examples.quote: By Friday the same crowd would turn on him.
examples.replacement: By Friday a crowd would be shouting for his death.
examples.why: The Gospels do not say the Palm Sunday crowd and the Friday crowd were the same people. A careful reader, or a skeptic, will catch it.

examples.quote: The verse says give thanks in all circumstances, not for all circumstances.
examples.replacement: The verse says give thanks in every circumstance, not for every circumstance.
examples.tell: Quotes a different translation from the passage printed above it
examples.why: The passage text on the card reads "in every circumstance"; the reflection quotes other wording as "the verse says".

structural_pattern: Every one of the 72 devotions is two paragraphs of about 60 to 80 words: paragraph one opens on an everyday image, paragraph two pivots with 'The verse ...' or 'This is ...', and the last sentence is a slogan. Read one a night and by the second week a family hears the mould. Thanksgiving week breaks the mould (one developed paragraph that follows the passage) and is far better for it. This cannot be fixed sentence by sentence; when pieces are revised, let some run as one paragraph, let some end on a question or on the passage, and vary where the verse comes in.

ten_worst.quote: Notice the psalm does not pretend fear away. The writer is scared and says so out loud. Then he does something small and brave. ten_worst.why: Three antitheses in one short card (Big Idea, this pair, and the promise pair in paragraph two) plus a quotable epigram about trust and hands.

ten_worst.quote: He is alive. And because he lives, the worst thing is never the last thing.
ten_worst.replacement: He is alive. And because he lives, death will not keep anyone who belongs to him.
ten_worst.why: Easter ends on an uncredited line usually attributed to Frederick Buechner.

ten_worst.quote: It does not mean you let them hurt you. It means you refuse to become bitter. It is the strongest, hardest, most God like thing a person can do.
ten_worst.replacement: It doesn't mean you let them hurt you, and if someone is hurting you, tell a grown-up you trust. It means you refuse to become bitter. It is hard, and it is what God is like.
ten_worst.why: Forced superlative triplet, missing hyphen, and no path to help for a child who is being harmed.

ten_worst.quote: Think about how amazing this is. The God who made the entire universe, who needs nothing, who was never born and never dies, chose to become a tiny baby. He had to be fed and held and taught to walk, just like you once were. The Maker of the stars learned to count them on his fingers.
ten_worst.replacement: The God who made the entire universe, who needs nothing, who was never born and never dies, chose to become a tiny baby. He had to be fed and held and taught to walk, just like you once were.
ten_worst.why: Announced amazement at the front and an invented, embroidered image at the back.

ten_worst.quote: The question is less try harder and more stay connected. Healthy roots, good fruit.
ten_worst.replacement: So the question to ask is whether you're staying connected, more than whether you're trying hard enough.

ten_worst.quote: That is the picture Jesus gives us of God. Not arms crossed. Arms open, running.
ten_worst.replacement: That is the picture Jesus gives us of God. His arms are not crossed. They are open, and He is running.
ten_worst.why: Fragment-stack kicker on one of the strongest pieces in the library.

ten_worst.quote: You can be scared and brave at the same time. In fact, that is the only kind of brave there is.
ten_worst.replacement: You can be scared and brave at the same time.
ten_worst.why: Epigram restating the title, the Big Idea and the previous sentence.

ten_worst.quote: Jesus is a shepherd who leads us and would die to keep us safe, and a shepherd does not drive his sheep from behind. [...] Most shepherds run when the wolf comes.
ten_worst.replacement: Jesus is a shepherd who leads us and would die to keep us safe. [...] The hired hand runs when the wolf comes.
ten_worst.why: A patched tail clause in the line a child repeats, and a misreading of John 10:12.

ten_worst.quote: Calling Jesus Lord is not a polite religious phrase. It is a surrender. It means he gets a say in our money, our anger, our screens, our marriages.
ten_worst.replacement: When we call Jesus Lord, we're giving him a say in our money, our anger, our screens, our marriages.
ten_worst.why: Straw position, hard-period antithesis, one-word verdict.

ten_worst.quote: Welcome the question. A faith that cannot be questioned cannot be trusted.
ten_worst.why: Chiasmus epigram and a stock line, tacked on after the paragraph had already earned its point.

for_james: These read as competent, warm, orthodox children's material, and almost none of it could only be yours. The Thanksgiving week is the exception and the model: it sounds like a father at a table. The surest way to lift the rest is for you to rewrite four or five of the devotions yourself, aloud, and let those set the ear for the others. No one else can supply the real remembered detail (a son's question at bedtime, what you actually say when one of the boys is afraid of the dark); I have not invented any and no fixer should.

Contractions: your Substack brief says 'contractions light'; VOICE-JAMES-BELL.md says prefer contractions where they make prose sound spoken. For pieces read aloud to children I have followed VOICE-JAMES-BELL.md and recommended contracting most of them. Say so if you want the family pages kept formal.

Your saved Substack profile and VOICE-JAMES-BELL.md disagree, and I have followed VOICE-JAMES-BELL.md: the profile asks for 2-4 sentence paragraphs, 'stacked landing lines', contrast lines and a line 'the reader screenshots', which is exactly the slogan-and-fragment habit that makes these devotions sound machine-made. I have not rewritten toward the profile.

Scripture translation: CLAUDE.md says ESV by default; every passage here is the Berean Standard Bible (the family validator enforces it, presumably for licensing). Nothing on the cards names the translation. Either name it once on the page or confirm the choice. Two reflections quote wording that is not in the BSB text printed above them (gratitude: 'in all circumstances'; screens-and-attention: 'noble'); fixes are in the findings.

Capital pronouns for God: family-devotions.json and the first forty or so of family-devotions-2.json write He/Him/His; from 'prayer' onward, and all of the seasonal file and the catechism, write he/him/his. It is a visible seam between two batches. Pick one. (The BSB text itself capitalises.)

Catechism structure: Part 5 (Q53-Q64) asks again, with different answers, eight questions already answered earlier (Q8/Q64 why God made you, Q11/Q56 what God requires, Q21/Q58 keeping the law, Q45/Q63 how the Spirit changes us, Q47/Q61 baptism, Q48/Q62 the Supper, Q49-50/Q53-54 prayer). A family memorising it will be asked the same question twice with two answers. Decide which answer stands.

Second-order doctrine in the catechism needs your eye. Baptism is called 'the sign God gives to mark his people' and a mark of 'God's covenant family' (Q47, Q61), which is covenantal language a Baptist reader may not expect; the Supper answers say 'we feed on him by faith' (Q48, Q62); Q9, Q39 and Q42 state sovereignty, perseverance and regeneration in their Reformed form. None of these says faithful churches differ. The Lord's Supper devotion does this well ('Christians have understood the Lord's Supper in different ways'); Q71 does it well for creation. Tell us where you land or we add one such line to each.

Q34 says grace alone 'split the church open in history'. If you mean the Reformation, say so in your own words ('This is the truth the Reformation was fought over'); I have only offered the cut, not the naming.

Q43: 'For anyone raised without a good father, this is the deepest healing there is.' I have softened the superlative. You are the one person who can say plainly what being told 'Abba' meant to a man raised without a father; one sentence from you here, if you want it there, would be worth more than any edit. It should not be written for you.

The Trinity devotion's apple activity (skin, fruit, seeds) is the kind of illustration your own Q76 warns parents against. I have proposed replacing it with reading and counting the names in Matthew 28:19.

Paths to help: the devotions on fear, anger, grief, suffering, church hurt and forgiveness carry a grown-ups link to /help. The seasonal file has no such field, so Thanksgiving day 6 (The Empty Chair), day 4 (which says 'there is no shame in asking for help' without saying where) and Advent day 7 have none; nor do catechism Q65, Q70 and Q75, which the commentary itself says are asked 'when a family is actually hurting'. That needs a small data and page change, not a wording change.

'Blessed' appears four times in the-beatitudes; all are the Beatitudes' own word, so I have left them. No other Forbidden Language word, no em-dash and no exclamation point occurs outside quoted Scripture. No biography, title, book count or one-directional politics appears anywhere in these four files.

Titles are in Title Case With Every Word Capitalised in the two devotion files and in ordinary title case in the seasonal file. Devotion ids are frozen; if any test or index matches on titles, the three title changes I suggest need the family index rebuilt.
apply_notes: Every finding's quote was checked to occur exactly once in the named file, id and field. Replace only inside that field.
After editing, rebuild the family index and run validate-family, validate-grow-voice and validate-no-emdash (not run by this audit, which was read-only).
Pattern A (contractions) and pattern G (intensifiers) are passes to make by ear across the files, not only the listed examples.
